source_ref: OSF dqw9f (public node; API reports no node licence): Studies In Main Text/Study 2 Data and Code/Study 2 Data no ID.sav (https://osf.io/download/hymb6/, sha256 390e7966...65b27f); Supplemental Studies/Study S1a Data.sav (https://osf.io/download/5p78v/, sha256 ceefe3a6...503f33), S1b (https://osf.io/download/8j3em/, sha256 55f1616c...e6e7ea), S1c (https://osf.io/download/2knxu/, sha256 4a5debaf...d9142e), S2a (https://osf.io/download/j7bu9/, sha256 64c2f427...3175ce), S2b (https://osf.io/download/6501ed786d1e89617115155a/, sha256 37cf92d0...ba05dd), S2c (https://osf.io/download/6501f901f3dcd16832ddd406/, sha256 77e72d25...e4732e) -- SPSS variable and value labels of IQbelief1T1/2T1/3T1 (Study 2, S1c, S2c) and IQbelief1T1/1T2/1T3/2T3 (S1a, S1b, S2a, S2b); the studies' own .sps syntax; data/wallace_2026_mindsets.py for the code derivation. Paper: Wallace, Murphy, Hernandez-Colmenares & Fujita (2026) JPSP 130(2) 291-307, doi:10.1037/pspi0000498.
note: Level 1, both label levels read in all seven .sav files (reused from the batch_647 wallace_2026_certain cache; full sha256 of all seven match the sibling records). CODE DERIVATION (data/wallace_2026_mindsets.py, iqbelief.csv spec): Study 2/S1c/S2c IQbelief{1,2,3}T1 -> IQbelief{1,2,3}, wave 1 (item = source name minus the T1 suffix); S1a/S1b/S2a/S2b IQbelief1T1 -> IQbelief1 wave 1, IQbelief1T2 -> IQbelief2 wave 1, IQbelief1T3 -> IQbelief1 wave 2, IQbelief2T3 -> IQbelief2 wave 2. This is a fixed named rename, not positional, and the one non-obvious leg (IQbelief1T2 -> IQbelief2) is confirmed by the file's own variable label, which carries item 2's wording (Your intelligence is something about you that you can't change very much.) in all four studies, and by the authors' syntax (compute IQT1=(IQbelief1T1+IQbelief1T2)/2 in S1a/S1b/S2a). Treated as data_labels, so no verification files. Corroboration anyway, route 9: all 25 study x source column x wave count vectors (resp 1..7) match live exactly, and within every study the vectors differ between items, e.g. Study 2 IQbelief1T1 17/63/156/55/232/236/79 vs IQbelief2T1 16/56/113/64/236/257/95 vs IQbelief3T1 25/91/187/71/194/202/68; S1a IQbelief1T2 -> IQbelief2 19/30/36/22/45/33/53; S2b IQbelief2T3 -> IQbelief2 wave 2 29/35/29/39/62/69/77. Live 11976 rows. NO RECODE: all seven studies label 1 = Strongly agree ... 7 = Strongly disagree and the live table has no itemcov_recoded. WORDING: identical across studies apart from apostrophe glyph and a lead-in. IQbelief1/2 labels use a straight apostrophe in S1a/S1b/S2a/S2b/S2c and a curly one (’) in Study 2/S1c; shipped straight (majority, 1967 of 3601 study-ids). IQbelief3 is curly in all three studies that carry it; shipped curly. Wave-2 labels (IQbelief1T3, IQbelief2T3) match the wave-1 wording. Several labels (IQbelief1T2 in S1a/S1b/S2a/S2b; IQbelief2T1 and IQbelief3T1 in S2c) begin 'Please rate the extent to which you agree with the following statement:' followed by blank lines; that lead-in is not attested for item 1 or for Study 2/S1c, so it is not placed in instructions (left blank) and is stripped from item_text. OPTIONS: Study 2 and S1c value labels name all seven points (Strongly agree, Agree, Somewhat agree, Neither agree nor disagree, Somewhat disagree, Disagree, Strongly disagree); S1a/S1b/S2a/S2b/S2c label only 1 = '1 - Strongly agree' and 7 = '7 - Strongly disagree', 2-6 carrying only their digit. resp 1/7 ship unprefixed (digit prefixes stripped); resp 2-6 ship the Study 2/S1c label prefixed 'Studies 2 and S1c (cov_study = 1, 4): ' (IRW's prefix) because the other studies' respondents saw only the number. Rights: Dweck's implicit-theories items; only a bare '(c) Carol Dweck' notice found on a third-party reproduction (a copyright notice, not a reserved right); no fee, permission, NC or redistribution clause located -- silence = permission. Not in instrument_rights_register.csv; no register row written.
public_note: Responses run 1 = Strongly agree to 7 = Strongly disagree, so a higher value means disagreeing that intelligence is fixed (a more growth-oriented belief); the intermediate labels (Agree ... Disagree) were shown only in Studies 2 and S1c (cov_study = 1, 4), and the other studies' respondents saw numbers at points 2-6.
